name: plan-china-high-council
description: The Chinese High Council (0.8.3): an alternative route next to the three planning chains (plan-mini-council, plan-medium-council, plan-high-council), not a replacement for any of them, with the shape of plan-high-council. It runs the planning stages with six proposers (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GLM-5.3 Flash, Tencent HY4 Preview, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiniMax M3), an alternatives stage (GLM-5.3, MiMo V2.6 Pro and Qwen 3.8 Max; every proposer also debates the architectures), one deep-dive seat (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and a layered review panel of twelve named judges in three layers: layer 1 GLM-5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiniMax M3, MiMo V2.6 Pro, Tencent HY4 Preview, StepFun Step 5 Preview; layer 2 DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, Qwen 3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro; layer 3 GLM-5.3 and Qwen 3.8 Max. Every proposer, alternatives seat, deep-dive seat and judge is a model from a Chinese lab. Tencent HY4 Preview and StepFun Step 5 Preview are preview models. Exactly these twelve judge seats vote; they are filled by nine models from seven companies, and the review panel counts nine labs, one per model, because a model that sits in two layers is one lab, not two. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GLM-5.3 Flash, Tencent HY4 Preview, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiniMax M3 and GLM-5.3 each both propose and judge, which is why "judging" is "all-roles". Every layer has at least two judges. A layer is asked only when every layer below it signed off, and a layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser and the climb starts again at layer 1; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. This chain allows 7 such overseer rounds (maxOverseerRounds) and, inside one round, 5 revisions of layer 1 and 3 of layer 2 (layerRevisions). When either limit is reached the run stops, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose: continue (it extends the limit that was reached; the run's spending limit still applies), or finish (the dispute stage and the handoff run and the result stays "not agreed"), or revise the draft yourself. answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria stage is answered through your Claude subscription (the Opus 5.5 seat, `provider: external`). The skeleton, build, revise, handoff and decider stages are answered by your Claude Code session (`provider: external`). A stage that waits for an external answer pauses the run with exit code 3 until it is answered. These Claude-backed stages are the only exceptions to the Chinese-model roster. Every API seat reasons at high, or at the model's own default where that is higher (the harness sends these no effort setting: GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3 Flash at max, Qwen 3.8 Max at xhigh); no Grok, no Kimi, no Mistral. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 384,000; MiMo V2.6 Pro, GLM-5.3 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max and GLM-5.3 131,072; Tencent HY4 Preview and StepFun Step 5 Preview 64,000. For MiniMax M3 no published limit was found, so the seat cap is 128,000. Dry run (0.8.3, prices of 2026-10-23, the dry run's assumed sizes): $18.64 expected (every overseer round ends after one climb through the layers) and an upper estimate of $175.72 (every allowed revision used in every overseer round), about $18.64 plus a Claude subscription. The upper estimate leaves out the in-pass re-asks (up to 2 per seat), up to 2 consecutive passes that re-ask a silent seat, the explicit asks of a silent judge, answer-back calls, the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices) and the larger prompt the top layer reads, so it is not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The upper estimate ($175.72) and the cheapest end ($12.87, one overseer round, the dry run's floor) are above the default cap of $7, the figure the dry run compares a chain with; on the command line your limit is the number you type. The Claude Desktop bundle's default Spend ceiling of $10 is a hard ceiling nobody can type above, so with that default this chain probably cannot finish (an inference from the dry run's floor, not a run): raise the ceiling setting first. This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run.
summary: Twelve judge seats, six proposers, all Chinese labs; criteria: Opus 5.5 subscription; writer and decider: the session.
